title: Flow Imaging Microscopy of Elastin-like Polymers
author: Eva Rose Balog
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vg9e3z6
materials: Within the Prime window, click Evacuate Syringe.

steps.title: Prepare ice bucket
steps.instruction: Fill a bucket with ice and keep it ready for samples, solvents, and focus beads to stay cold.

steps.title: Power on and launch software
steps.instruction: Turn on the computer, then the FlowCam, and open the Visual Spreadsheet software.

steps.title: Sonicate flow cell
steps.instruction: Place the flow cell in de‑ionized (DI) water and sonicate for 180 seconds.

steps.title: Inspect and clean flow cell
steps.instruction: Click the Setup | Focus icon to open the Setup and Focus Mode window, examine the view for contamination, bubbles or glass imperfections, and return to the cleaning procedure (step 5) if needed; wait to see whether imperfections are mistakenly captured as particles.

steps.title: Prime with sample solvent
steps.instruction: Add the solvent used to resuspend the sample (not the sample itself) to a pipette tip, go to Setup > Pump > Prime, and aspirate 0.5 mL.

steps.title: Set context parameters
steps.instruction: Click the Context icon, load the desired context file (e.g., 11-02-2018-Buffer#4-Run#1.post.ctx), and set the minimum ESD diameter to 2 µm.

steps.title: Weigh freeze‑dried ELP
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of freeze‑dried elastin‑like polymer, typically 0.8–1.5 mg per experiment.

steps.title: Resuspend ELP
steps.instruction: Calculate the solvent volume (e.g., to obtain ~1.4 mg/mL, use at least 1 mL; for 1.6 mg freeze‑dried ELP add 1.12 mL sterile‑filtered, ice‑cold H₂O), add the solvent, chill on ice and pipette up/down until no solid remains; keep on ice during cleaning/focusing, then allow to warm to room temperature for at least 10 min before running.

steps.title: Mark pipette tip
steps.instruction: Place a 1 mL pipette tip on the top of the flow‑cell tubing and draw a line about halfway up the tip with a Sharpie.

steps.title: Prime with water three times
steps.instruction: In Visual Spreadsheet go to Setup > Pump > Prime and aspirate 0.5 mL DI water; repeat this aspiration two more times, confirming that the liquid level drops, checking for bubbles downstream or air pockets in the syringe, and returning to step 5 for cleaning if flow is blocked.

steps.title: Maintain liquid level
steps.instruction: Add DI water to the pipette tip until the liquid level is above the Sharpie mark; keep the level above the mark throughout operation unless the flow cell is removed for cleaning or storage.

steps.title: Install optical components
steps.instruction: Install the 20X objective, 20X collimator, and the 0.5 mL syringe according to the FlowCam manual.

steps.title: Install flow cell
steps.instruction: Install the flow cell following the FlowCam manual instructions.

steps.title: Clean flow cell if needed
steps.instruction: If the flow cell is not clean, fill it with isopropyl alcohol and sonicate again; repeat as many times as necessary. If required, a detergent wash may be used, but rinse thoroughly afterward because detergents can affect protein behavior.

steps.title: Verify flow after cleaning
steps.instruction: When the flow cell is clean, add water and aspirate again to confirm acceptable flow.

steps.title: Add focus beads and set flow
steps.instruction: Return to the Setup and Focus Mode window, add 100 µL focus beads, open the Pump Control window, set the flow rate to 0.030 mL/min, and visually confirm that beads are flowing through the flow cell.

steps.title: Manually focus on beads
steps.instruction: Gently adjust the position of the flow cell to manually bring the beads into focus.

steps.title: Run autofocus assistant
steps.instruction: In the Setup and Focus Mode window choose Tools > Autofocus, follow the Auto Focus Assistant steps, and accept the pop‑up indicating success; if autofocus fails, add more beads and repeat.

steps.title: Start AutoImage acquisition
steps.instruction: Click the AutoImage icon, select “Stop when user terminates experiment or fluid is aspirated,” assign a run name (e.g., date‑solvent‑run #), and click Save to begin the run.

steps.title: Perform practice run
steps.instruction: Run a practice acquisition to check for flow problems, glass imperfections, and proper particle capture; examine the Capture Y vs Capture X scatter plot, particle edge trace, and binary image overlays, and adjust particle capture and segmentation threshold context settings as needed.

steps.title: Aspirate after run
steps.instruction: After the run finishes, aspirate again and add solvent if necessary.

steps.title: Load sample aliquot
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the sample to the pipette tip.

steps.title: Repeat sample loading
steps.instruction: Add another 100 µL of sample and repeat steps 22‑24 (load sample, run acquisition, aspirate) as many times as desired.

steps.title: Flush after all samples
steps.instruction: When all samples have been run, add DI water and aspirate again to flush the system.

steps.title: Remove and sonicate flow cell
steps.instruction: Remove the flow cell from the holder, sonicate it again in DI water (repeat step 3), and return it to the box labeled “proteins only.”

steps.title: Inspect flow cell for damage
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the 50 µm flow cell for cracks or other damage; if none are found, proceed to data analysis.

steps.title: Open experiment list file
steps.instruction: In Visual Spreadsheet open the .lst file for the experiment and click the “Open View” button to display the View window.

steps.title: Filter images by similarity
steps.instruction: Go to Filter > Like selected particles (Statistical) to re‑sort all images by their filter score based on similarity to the selected images.

steps.title: Delete bead images
steps.instruction: Manually select all bead images and choose Edit > Delete Images Selected.

steps.title: Save cleaned image list
steps.instruction: Choose File > Save As List… to save the remaining images as a new .lst file.
